ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are moving to significantly expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, seeking to add over 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The development marks a major escalation in one of the most closely watched music copyright cases involving generative AI. The case has significant implications for how AI training on commercial recordings will be treated under copyright law.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across approximately 30,000 works. The move mirrors parallel action against Suno and signals that major labels are using discovery to build significantly larger infringement claims than initially filed. The case is a key battleground for AI music training practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors pursuing copyright claims over Meta's Llama AI model have taken the unusual step of suing Meta's AI scientists directly, rather than limiting claims to the company itself. The move represents a significant shift in litigation strategy and could have broad implications for individual liability in AI copyright disputes. The case centres on allegations that Llama was trained on books without authorisation.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought by Disney and Warner Bros., allowing the case to proceed. The suit alleges MiniMax's AI system was trained on or used copyrighted content without permission. The ruling keeps alive a significant test case for AI copyright liability involving major entertainment IP holders.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will introduce an AI policy after a nominated anthology, Stardust, was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. Publishers Weekly reports the withdrawal prompted the prestigious comics awards to formalise its approach to AI-assisted work. The case highlights growing pressure on awards bodies and publishers to define and enforce AI content standards.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's latest legal action is prompting broader debate about whether a performer's voice can be protected under existing copyright and trademark law in the age of AI voice cloning.

ip_further_links.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_further_links.summary: An artist has filed suit against the US Copyright Office after it refused to register an AI-enhanced photograph, escalating legal debate over the threshold of human authorship required for copyright protection of AI-assisted works.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA argues that the EU's existing copyright framework is creating obstacles for AI development in Europe, potentially hampering the continent's competitiveness against US and Chinese AI industries.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering regulatory measures to address AI services that summarise news content without compensation to publishers, framing the issue as unlicensed commercial use of journalistic work.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are calling on the government to resist any weakening of copyright protections in the face of AI industry lobbying, amid ongoing national policy consultations.

ip_further_links.title: Matt Comyn urges Australia to resolve AI copyright standoff
ip_further_links.summary: Commonwealth Bank of Australia CEO Matt Comyn has publicly called for Australia to find a resolution to the ongoing standoff between AI developers and rights holders over copyright, warning economic consequences of inaction.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is taking an active role in shaping AI copyright policy, seeking to ensure creators are compensated when their works are used to train or power AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI-driven research tools is transforming user behaviour in academic publishing, questioning whether publishers are adapting quickly enough to remain relevant.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis argues that accumulating copyright litigation exposure represents a systemic legal risk that could significantly dampen investor confidence and growth projections for generative AI companies.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia Weighs AI Royalty Agency to Protect Creators' Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia is considering establishing a dedicated AI royalty agency to ensure creators receive compensation when their work is used in AI training or output, as part of broader digital copyright modernisation efforts.
